questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I opted for Amsterdam as my exchange destination during my BA mainly because it's close to home in Denmark. The proximity made it convenient for travel, allowing me to easily explore a new city without being too far from familiar surroundings.

Additionally, Amsterdam's renowned cultural diversity and dynamic atmosphere appealed to me. I was eager to immerse myself in a vibrant city with a distinct vibe and rich history, all while being just a stone's throw away from Denmark.

questions.answer: It wasn't really something I did intentionally I just chose housing based on my needs.

questions.answer: I really enjoyed it, as the on-campus housing is quite far from center but it is not as social.

Additional comments:

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a little bit confusing because I thought there would be some kind of system of wishing for courses but I just got the courses that I signed up for. I took a minor, which was super convenient, because I then was sure to not have courses which overlapped. Also, then you are with the same people all the time which allows you to get some new friends.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The administration is pretty attentive and answered my mails pretty fast.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: As I wrote, I got the courses that I registered for and it didn't seem like there was a chance of not getting the ones you wish for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The academic level is very high at the VU, so be sure to pick something that you care about and is interested in so that you don't have a harder time than necessary. Also, whatever you do, do not take the course "finance" at this university, as EVERYONE fails this course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: At VU, undertaking a minor in Peace and Conflict Studies proved to be intellectually invigorating. The program fostered vibrant discussions among a diverse student body, facilitated by competent professors who upheld high academic standards. Each course demanded rigorous engagement, challenging us to delve into historical and contemporary issues with depth and nuance. This was not a university where one could afford to slack off – rather, it was a place where dedication and critical thinking were paramount, shaping future leaders in the pursuit of peace.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty much same same. There were a lot of guest lectures which I liked.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Minor in Peace and Conflict studies. 

Philosophy and the Ethics of Political Violence: Peace, War and Terrorism
Conflict and Peacebuilding: Local and Global Perspectives
The Law and Politics of Fencing the Use of Force
Peace and Conflict: From Theory to Practice
Political Violence and the Human Condition

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Don't expect to have a "chill academic" year because it is high level. 
2. Amsterdam is a costly city to live in, both when it comes to housing, eating out and going out. Although it is cheaper in grocery stores than in Denmark. 
3. find housing before going on exchange in Amsterdam or you might as well stay home.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: This is a very nice university with great and competent professors and smart students.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living abroad in general was very fun and trying a new type of study form was also rewarding.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Money and finding dutch friends.
